raw_plan.interpretation: One acquisition email for the selected solution-aware technical founder audience. Because the reader relationship is unknown and no recipient has been qualified, the email will make an audience-level case for inspecting Fathom's single-page dashboard rather than assume the recipient currently uses GA4 or has suffered a specific failure. The primary next action is the documented live demo, a low-friction self-serve evaluation.

intent.desired_action: Get the reader to inspect the live Fathom dashboard and decide whether its one-page view surfaces the basic website metrics they care about.

raw_plan.reader: A technically minded founder who manages their own website analytics and wants basic traffic answers without navigating layers of reports.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A technical founder who built the site himself and gave up on GA4 somewhere around the third Explore report
raw_plan.reader_scope: Write at audience level because no companies or recipients have been qualified. Do not state that the recipient currently uses GA4, has installed a consent banner, distrusts their numbers, or has attempted a migration.
raw_plan.promise: Fathom puts the basic website signals a technical founder regularly checks on one live, single-page dashboard.
raw_plan.orientation: Fathom is a hosted, cookieless website analytics service that shows live and total visitors, top pages, referrers, countries, devices, events and UTM campaigns on a single real-time dashboard.
raw_plan.arc: Move directly from the familiar difficulty of retrieving basic analytics answers to a concrete, read-only inspection of Fathom's alternative interface.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: There is exactly one email, so it must stand alone. The primary argument uses the strongest addressed product/problem fit: a single page containing the metrics this audience reports difficulty finding. The live demo is preferable to asking an unknown reader to install a script or enter a card because it lets them inspect the relevant interface before deciding whether a trial is worthwhile. The brief does not claim that Fathom is measured as easier than GA4; it asks the reader to judge the documented dashboard directly.

emails.selection_reason: The audience is solution-aware and reports difficulty reaching top pages, referrers and a real-time view. Fathom's documented single-page dashboard directly addresses that need, and the public live demo lets an unqualified reader evaluate the interface without installation or a sales call.
emails.target_audience: A technical founder who built the site himself and gave up on GA4 somewhere around the third Explore report
emails.job: Earn a self-serve inspection of the live dashboard so the reader can decide whether Fathom presents the basic website signals they want in a usable view.
emails.single_idea: Instead of navigating through layers of analytics reports for routine answers, the reader can inspect live visitors, top pages, referrers and other core website metrics together on Fathom's single-page dashboard.
emails.felt_need: I want to see which pages people visit, where they came from and what is happening right now without digging through sub-menus.
emails.status_quo: Technically minded site operators report using Google Analytics for their sites while struggling to retrieve basic information such as top pages, referrers and a real-time view.
emails.why_it_fails: For the basic questions these operators ask, GA4's reported interface structure makes the relevant information difficult to find quickly.
emails.mechanism: Fathom concentrates live visitors, total visitors, pageviews, top pages, referrers, countries, devices, browsers, events and UTM campaigns on a single page. The reader can click through the public live dashboard to inspect that layout before installing anything.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: A separate documented concern for this audience is recurring cookie-banner and privacy administration. Fathom's cookieless operation and stated GDPR treatment support a distinct acquisition argument, while the trial can be run alongside existing analytics to evaluate it without requiring an immediate replacement decision.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: A founder can run website analytics without analytics cookies or a GDPR cookie-consent notice, then evaluate Fathom alongside any analytics already in place.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: I want website analytics without adding cookie-banner administration to every site I run.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Operators describe using cookie-based analytics together with recurring consent-banner and privacy administration.
alternative_arguments.why_it_fails: Analytics cookies create the need for consent handling, leaving the operator with ongoing banner and compliance work.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Fathom does not use cookies and states that it does not require a cookie consent notice to comply with GDPR. Its seven-day trial can run alongside existing analytics; a card is required, billing begins after the trial, and Fathom emails before that happens.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: privacy administration is an unavoidable part of having website analytics. After: a documented cookieless option can be tested alongside the current setup, without first committing to a full switch.
must_not_say: Do not claim that every jurisdiction or every website can remove every consent notice; the evidence specifically supports Fathom Analytics and its stated GDPR treatment.
Do not claim that cookieless tracking recovers a measured percentage of visitors or produces more accurate totals.
Do not say the recipient currently has a cookie banner, loses traffic data, or uses GA4.
Do not omit that the seven-day trial requires a card and renews automatically unless cancelled.
alternative_arguments.objection: Testing another analytics product may sound like committing to a migration before knowing whether it fits.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether Fathom's cookieless analytics is suitable enough to replace or complement the reader's current approach.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The seven-day trial lets the reader add Fathom to a site and run it alongside existing analytics; the card is not charged until the trial ends, and Fathom emails before billing starts.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The trial does not establish a quantified improvement in traffic visibility, accuracy, or business results, and it requires adding Fathom to a site.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame the practical possibility of website analytics without analytics-cookie consent administration; avoid fear, legal absolutes and claims about recovered traffic.

emails.belief_shift: Before: getting routine traffic answers still means navigating a complex analytics interface. After: Fathom offers a concrete one-page alternative the reader can inspect immediately and judge for themselves.
must_not_say: Do not claim Fathom has been measured as easier, faster or more accurate than GA4.
Do not promise trustworthy, complete or corrected traffic counts; bot filtering and real-time display do not establish accuracy against a baseline.
Do not say the recipient currently uses GA4, has lost visitors to a consent banner, distrusts their data, or previously failed to migrate.
Do not use the single-source claim that cookie banners make 30–50% of visitors disappear.
Do not introduce cookie compliance, EU infrastructure, integrations, GA4 importing, pricing, traffic-spike policies, site allowances or data retention; they are separate arguments.
Do not call the public dashboard a live sales demo or imply that a salesperson will attend; Fathom does not offer live demos or sales calls.
Do not claim exclusivity or that competitors cannot provide similar metrics.
emails.objection: The reader may reasonably wonder whether 'simple analytics' hides the metrics they actually need.
emails.tone: Blunt, concise and self-assured, with a practical invitation to verify the claim rather than sales pressure.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Fathom's dashboard surfaces the routine website metrics the reader needs clearly enough to justify a trial.
emails.next_step_value: The destination is a clickable live dashboard where the reader can inspect Fathom's single-page presentation of core website metrics without a sales call or account setup.
emails.next_step_limit: The public demo shows the dashboard experience but does not test the reader's own traffic, installation, migration, accuracy, or compatibility with their site.
emails.subject_strategy: Signal relief from report navigation by naming the concrete basic answers available in one view; do not use generic simplicity claims or pretend to know the recipient's current setup.

raw_plan.voice_notes: Use short declarative paragraphs and plain product language. Address the reader as 'you' and speak as 'we' or 'Fathom.' Avoid hype, generic conversion language and an individual sender persona.

events.body:
Fathom is website analytics that puts your core traffic signals on one page. You can see live and total visitors, pageviews, top pages and referrers together.

The dashboard also includes countries, devices, browsers, events and UTM campaigns. Simple does not mean stripping away the routine metrics you may need.

Inspect how the metrics are presented, move around the dashboard and decide whether it gives you the view you want.

events.preview_text: Run Fathom alongside your current analytics before deciding whether it fits.
events.body:
Fathom doesn’t use analytics cookies. That means a site using Fathom Analytics doesn’t need a cookie consent notice to comply with GDPR.

Fathom is a website analytics service built to provide analytics without tracking visitors with cookies.

You can run it alongside any analytics already on your site. That lets you inspect Fathom on your own traffic before deciding whether it should replace or complement your current approach.

The **7-day free trial** requires a card. It isn’t charged until the trial ends, and we’ll email you before billing starts. The subscription renews automatically unless you cancel in your account settings.

readers.persona:
Selected audience (explicit constraints): A technical founder who built the site himself and gave up on GA4 somewhere around the third Explore report.
The context and problem reports below describe observed members of this market, not established experiences or installed tools of this recipient. The campaign request controls which job this email addresses; do not require a link to an unrequested integration in your doubts or click requirements.
Observed context (grounded; applicability must be checked): Individual, technically-minded operators who run their own sites' Google Analytics setup describe difficulty getting quick, basic answers (top pages, referrers, a real-time view) out of the tool, and several describe no longer trusting what the dashboard tells them about their own site's traffic.
Source: https://blog.opencagedata.com/post/privacy-update-switching-from-google-analytics-to-fathom; quote: I kept finding myself lost in sub-menu 27 when all I wanted was basic information.
Source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=34392217; quote: It is so hard to find basic info like what pages are people most looking at, a realtime view, what are all the domains referring people to me, etc.
Source: https://www.indiehackers.com/post/from-building-client-websites-to-launching-my-own-saas-and-why-i-stopped-trusting-ga4-cXTyy2KRzwrhJUkW7561; quote: At some point I realized something uncomfortable: I don’t actually know what’s happening on my own websites.
Problem context: Two separate site operators, in separate venues, report that GA4's interface makes it hard to quickly find basic information such as top pages, referrers, and a real-time view.; source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=34392217
Problem context: One founder reports that adding a cookie consent banner to his own sites caused a reported share of visitors to disappear from the analytics data. [Source limits: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.]; source: https://www.indiehackers.com/post/from-building-client-websites-to-launching-my-own-saas-and-why-i-stopped-trusting-ga4-cXTyy2KRzwrhJUkW7561
Problem context: One founder reports not trusting or understanding the real traffic on his own self-run websites, describing the data as never feeling real. [Source limits: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.]; source: https://www.indiehackers.com/post/from-building-client-websites-to-launching-my-own-saas-and-why-i-stopped-trusting-ga4-cXTyy2KRzwrhJUkW7561
Problem context: Two separate operators describe recurring GDPR/ePrivacy and cookie-banner administration as a burden tied to running analytics on their own sites.; source: https://www.indiehackers.com/post/from-building-client-websites-to-launching-my-own-saas-and-why-i-stopped-trusting-ga4-cXTyy2KRzwrhJUkW7561
Problem context: Two operators who self-hosted their own analytics report wanting to stop maintaining it themselves, either moving to a hosted SaaS or actively looking for an alternative. [Source limits: Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability.]; source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=29665907
readers.what_it_sells: Fathom sells website analytics software that would replace digging through GA4 with one dashboard for live visitors, traffic totals, top pages, referrers and related metrics.
readers.biggest_doubt: Nothing material stops me from inspecting a no-signup public dashboard; my later doubt would be whether using Fathom on my own site is easy enough to justify changing my current setup.
fixes: Rewrite "Simple does not mean stripping away the routine metrics you may need." as "You still get countries, devices, browsers, events and UTM campaigns." The existing line is defensive and slower to parse.

Combine "Inspect how the metrics are presented, move around the dashboard and decide whether it gives you the view you want." with the CTA as "Open the live dashboard and see whether this is the view you wanted from GA4."
